The simulation is a 2D axisymmetric spray combustion of liquid n-dodecane in a cylindrical chamber, solved with reactingParcelFoam in OpenFOAM.
The chamber is a straight cylinder 0.2 m long and 0.1 m in diameter, modeled as a half-cross-section with the axis of symmetry as a boundary.
The mesh is generated with BlockMesh: 100 cells in the axial direction by 50 cells in the radial direction, graded tighter near the axis (r = 0) and near the injector face (x = 0).
The turbulence model is k-epsilon.
The spray injection uses the cone injection model at the inlet centre, with a mass flow rate of 0.002 kg/s, initial droplet temperature of 300 K, and a Rosin-Rammler droplet size distribution with dMean of 50e-6 m. The Rosin-Rammler spread parameter n is set to 2.4 (assumed default, not specified in the task brief; flag as an assumption in the dictionary). The cone half-angle is 10 degrees (assumed default, not specified in the task brief; flag as an assumption). No velocity key is set in the spray dictionary; the mass flow rate governs injection.
The gas-phase inlet boundary conditions are: U = (10 0 0) m/s, T = 800 K, p = fixedValue 101325 Pa, species mass fractions Y_O2 = 0.233 and Y_N2 = 0.767, k = 0.375 m²/s², epsilon = 5.4 s⁻¹. The k and epsilon values are derived from a 5 percent turbulence intensity and a length scale of 0.07 times the chamber diameter (0.007 m).
The outlet boundary conditions are: p uses totalPressure with p0 = 101325 Pa; U, T, all species mass fractions, k, and epsilon use zeroGradient.
The outer cylindrical wall boundary conditions are: T = fixedValue 400 K, U = noSlip, and p, k, epsilon, and all species mass fractions use zeroGradient.
The axis boundary uses symmetry conditions for all fields.
The combustion model is a two-step global reaction mechanism with JANAF thermodynamic data. Step 1 is C12H26 + 18.5 O2 = 12 CO + 13 H2O (fast, low activation energy). Step 2 is CO + 0.5 O2 = CO2 (slower, higher activation energy). The tracked species are C12H26, O2, N2, CO, H2O, and CO2.
The initial condition inside the chamber is: U = 0 everywhere, T = 800 K, p = 101325 Pa, Y_O2 = 0.233, Y_N2 = 0.767, k = 0, epsilon = 0.
The simulation runs to an end time of 0.05 s with an adjustable time step and maxCo of 0.7. The write interval is 0.001 s, producing 50 output time directories.
